title: Segment-aware callsite metrics and policy-driven sanitization for streamed outputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Current streaming telemetry ties metrics and traces to request-level primitives which loses granularity for long-lived streamed responses and function/tool call boundaries. This makes it hard to diagnose per-segment latency spikes, attribute cost to tool invocations inside streams, and safely log streamed content without leaking PII.

Goal: Emit fine-grained, segment-aware metrics and tracing spans for streamed responses that: (1) attach callsite and tool-calling context to each segment, (2) include a lightweight provenance handshake between streaming runtime and tool adapters, and (3) apply configurable, policy-driven sanitization at segment boundaries so logs/metrics are scrubbed before persistence. Provide a compatibility shim for older SDKs that expect single-chunk semantics.

Scope: Design and implement runtime changes to: segment-id generation, per-segment telemetry envelope, tracing handshake for tool/function calls emitted mid-stream, scrub-level propagation, and a small compatibility layer in the API gateway to map legacy chunking semantics. Implement dashboard tiles and alerts in the Console for segment-level latency P50/P95, per-segment error propagation from tool calls, and scrubbed token samples.

Out-of-scope: UI redesigns beyond dashboard tiles, full SDK rewrites (we will provide shims), and changes to model serving kernels.
acceptance_criteria: Each streamed segment emits a telemetry envelope containing: segment_id, fragment_index, token_range_start, token_range_end, parent_request_id, span_id, callsite_labels, scrub_level.
Tool/function invocations that occur mid-stream create a child span with a tool_call_id and surface tool_error metrics; spans are stitchable to overall request trace in Console traces view.
Sanitization policy applied at segment boundary removes or masks PII according to configured scrub_level (none/minimal/full) before logs or long-term metrics are persisted.
Backward compatibility: SDKs that send legacy single-chunk streams are mapped to segment_id=legacy-<request_id> and still emit the envelope so dashboards and alerts remain consistent.
Dashboard tiles for segment P50/P95 latency, per-segment tool error rate, and token throughput are visible in Console-Streaming > Segment Insights by default for runtime-1.19 canary customers.

End-to-end test demonstrating: a streaming request invoking a tool mid-stream, with spans visible in trace, sanitized logged content in the log store, and correct segment-level metrics in Prometheus/Grafana dashboard.
Performance: no more than 3% added p50 token latency for standard short streams (<= 256 tokens) in canary environment under normal load.
comments: 2026-02-18 - AM: Created ticket after on-call incident where long-running stream masked tool timeout errors. Initial draft of telemetry envelope attached in Confluence.
2026-02-22 - RP: Proposal reviewed with runtime and infra. Agreed to use 64-bit segment_id (rand + monotonic) and add fragment_index for ordering. Decided scrub_level enum rather than freeform tags.
2026-02-27 - PM (Liam Chen): Prioritize console tiles for segment latency and tool error rate; these are key for customer SLOs. Marking as P1.

2026-03-03 - ENG: Prototype implemented in branch feat/segment-telemetry. Initial microbench shows ~1.8% p50 overhead for short streams. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2437

2026-03-05 - Security (Nina Gomez): Requested threat model and data flow for sanitization; recommended we avoid sending raw token text to metrics pipelines even transiently. We'll use hashed token samples for QA only.
2026-03-08 - RP: Added compatibility shim design to map legacy single-chunk clients to segment envelopes. Edge case: intermittent SDK reconnections — will dedupe by request_id + sequence number.

2026-03-12 - AM: Validated end-to-end test run on canary. Tool callspan is visible in traces, and sanitized logs show masked emails and SSNs per policy. Preparing rollout plan for canary cohort (5% orgs) next week.
Follow-ups: add observability playbook doc for SRE on how to use segment insights to troubleshoot streaming regressions.
